name: Transformer Encoder Block
summary: Stack of multi-head self-attention and position-wise feed-forward networks with residual connections and layer normalization.
description: The Transformer Encoder maps an input sequence of symbol representations to a sequence of continuous representations. Each encoder layer contains a multi-head self-attention sub-layer and a position-wise fully connected feed-forward sub-layer, both surrounded by residual connections and layer normalization.
math: Z = LayerNorm(x + MultiHead(x, x, x)), Output = LayerNorm(Z + FFN(Z))
problem: Sequential computational bottleneck of recurrent models (RNNs/LSTMs) preventing parallelized training across long sequence lengths.
solution: Eliminate recurrence entirely in favor of self-attention mechanisms that process all sequence positions in parallel.

pros: Full sequence parallelization during training
Constant path length between arbitrary positions O(1)
Scales effectively to massive parameters
cons: Quadratic computational and memory complexity O(N^2) with sequence length
Requires positional encodings to preserve spatial sequence order

papers: Attention Is All You Need (Vaswani et al., 2017)
codeSnippet:
class TransformerEncoderLayer(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, d_model, nhead, dim_feedforward):
        super().__init__()
        self.self_attn = MultiheadAttention(d_model, nhead)
        self.linear1 = nn.Linear(d_model, dim_feedforward)
        self.linear2 = nn.Linear(dim_feedforward, d_model)
        self.norm1 = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.norm2 = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)

name: Transformer Decoder Block
summary: Autoregressive generation block combining masked self-attention, encoder-decoder cross-attention, and feed-forward sub-layers.
description: The Transformer Decoder generates target sequences autoregressively. In addition to the multi-head self-attention and feed-forward sub-layers found in the encoder, the decoder inserts a third sub-layer: multi-head cross-attention over the encoder output. Self-attention is masked to prevent attending to future positions.
math: Z_1 = LayerNorm(x + MaskedMultiHead(x)), Z_2 = LayerNorm(Z_1 + CrossAttention(Z_1, K_enc, V_enc)), Output = LayerNorm(Z_2 + FFN(Z_2))
problem: Information leakage from future tokens during autoregressive target sequence training.
solution: Masked multi-head self-attention with upper-triangular causal masking.

pros: Autoregressive causal generation capability
Cross-attention seamlessly bridges encoder representations to target tokens
cons: Increased key-value caching memory overhead during decoding

papers: Attention Is All You Need (Vaswani et al., 2017)
codeSnippet:
class TransformerDecoderLayer(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, d_model, nhead):
        super().__init__()
        self.self_attn = MultiheadAttention(d_model, nhead)
        self.multihead_attn = MultiheadAttention(d_model, nhead)
        self.norm1 = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)
        self.norm2 = nn.LayerNorm(d_model)

name: Scaled Dot-Product Attention
summary: Core mathematical attention mechanism scaling query-key inner products by the square root of key dimension size.
description: Scaled Dot-Product Attention computes weights over values based on the inner product of queries and keys. Scaling by 1/sqrt(d_k) prevents softmax gradient vanishing at large dimensions.
math: Attention(Q, K, V) = Softmax( (Q * K^T) / sqrt(d_k) ) * V
problem: Unscaled dot products at large key dimensions (d_k) push the softmax function into regions with extremely small gradients.
solution: Scale dot product by 1/sqrt(d_k) to maintain unit variance before softmax exponentiation.

pros: Extremely fast matrix multiplication on modern GPUs
Direct dynamic routing between arbitrary sequence elements
cons: Memory footprint grows quadratically with sequence length O(N^2)

papers: Attention Is All You Need (Vaswani et al., 2017)

name: Multi-Head Attention
summary: Projects queries, keys, and values into multiple h subspaces to attend to information at different positions concurrently.
description: Multi-Head Attention allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions. Instead of performing a single attention function with d_model-dimensional keys, values, and queries, linear projections are used to project queries, keys, and values h times.
math: MultiHead(Q, K, V) = Concat(head_1, ..., head_h) * W^O, head_i = Attention(Q*W_i^Q, K*W_i^K, V*W_i^V)
problem: Single-headed attention averages out attention distributions across multiple semantic relationship types.
solution: Project representations into h parallel heads, allowing separate attention channels for syntax, positioning, and semantics.

pros: Attends to multiple semantic relationships concurrently
Maintains constant computational cost by reducing head projection dimension d_k = d_model / h
cons: Requires head splitting and transposition memory shuffling overhead

papers: Attention Is All You Need (Vaswani et al., 2017)
codeSnippet:
class MultiHeadAttention(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, d_model, n_heads):
        super().__init__()
        self.d_k = d_model // n_heads
        self.h = n_heads
        self.q_linear = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model)
        self.k_linear = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model)
        self.v_linear = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model)
        self.out_proj = nn.Linear(d_model, d_model)

name: Self-Attention Mechanism
summary: Attention mechanism where query, key, and value vectors originate from the same input sequence.
description: Self-attention, sometimes called intra-attention, is an attention mechanism relating different positions of a single sequence in order to compute a representation of the sequence.
math: Q = X * W_Q, K = X * W_K, V = X * W_V
problem: Capturing long-range contextual dependencies within a single sequence without recurrent accumulation.
solution: Allow each token in the sequence to attend directly to every other token in the sequence.

pros: Direct O(1) pairwise interaction between all sequence elements
Captures global context in a single layer
cons: Permutation invariant without explicit positional encoding

papers: Attention Is All You Need (Vaswani et al., 2017)
codeSnippet:
# Self-attention query, key, value derivation from single input tensor X
q = self.q_proj(X)
k = self.k_proj(X)
v = self.v_proj(X)

name: Cross-Attention Mechanism
summary: Attention mechanism where queries originate from decoder targets while keys and values originate from encoder outputs.
description: Cross-attention enables the decoder sequence to attend to representations generated by the encoder. Queries come from the previous decoder layer, while keys and values come from the output of the encoder.
math: Q = Decoder_X * W_Q, K = Encoder_Z * W_K, V = Encoder_Z * W_V
problem: Conditioning sequence generation on source sequence representations in sequence-to-sequence tasks.
solution: Inject encoder context vectors as keys and values into the decoder multi-head attention layers.

pros: Direct alignment between source and target sequence tokens
Crucial for translation and multimodal alignment
cons: Requires cached encoder key-value representations during decoding

papers: Attention Is All You Need (Vaswani et al., 2017)
codeSnippet:
# Cross-attention queries from decoder, keys/values from encoder memory
q = self.q_proj(decoder_hidden)
k = self.k_proj(encoder_output)
v = self.v_proj(encoder_output)

name: Position-Wise Feed-Forward Network
summary: Two linear transformations with a GELU/ReLU activation in between applied to each position separately and identically.
description: The Position-Wise Feed-Forward Network consists of two linear transformations with a non-linear activation function in between. It processes representations at each position independently and identically.
problem: Attention layers only perform linear combinations of values; non-linear feature transformation is required.
solution: Add two-layer dense network expanding representation dimension (typically 4x d_model) followed by non-linear projection.

pros: Introduces strong non-linear capacity
Processes sequence tokens in parallel
cons: Accounts for ~66% of total Transformer parameter parameters

papers: Attention Is All You Need (Vaswani et al., 2017)

name: Positional Encoding
summary: Sinusoidal or learned vector added to token embeddings to inject sequence order information.
description: Since the Transformer architecture contains no recurrence or convolution, it is permutation invariant. Positional encodings add trigonometric functions (sine and cosine of different frequencies) or learned embeddings to input representations to supply positional context.
problem: Attention mechanisms are order-agnostic (permutation invariant) without explicit sequence index information.
solution: Add fixed sinusoidal or learned position vectors to token embeddings.

pros: Fixed sinusoidal encodings allow extrapolation to sequence lengths unseen during training
Zero additional parameter overhead
cons: Learned positional encodings cannot extrapolate beyond max training context window

papers: Attention Is All You Need (Vaswani et al., 2017)
codeSnippet:
class PositionalEncoding(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, d_model, max_len=5000):
        super().__init__()
        pe = torch.zeros(max_len, d_model)
        position = torch.arange(0, max_len, dtype=torch.float).unsqueeze(1)
        div_term = torch.exp(torch.arange(0, d_model, 2).float() * (-math.log(10000.0) / d_model))
        pe[:, 0::2] = torch.sin(position * div_term)
        pe[:, 1::2] = torch.cos(position * div_term)
        self.register_buffer('pe', pe.unsqueeze(0))

name: Layer Normalization (LayerNorm)
summary: Normalizes activations across the feature channel dimension for each individual sequence token.
description: Unlike Batch Normalization which normalizes across the batch dimension, Layer Normalization computes mean and variance across feature dimensions for each sequence token independently, enabling stable batch-size independent training.
math: LN(x) = (x - mu) / sqrt(sigma^2 + epsilon) * gamma + beta
problem: Internal covariate shift and batch-size dependency of Batch Normalization in variable-length sequence models.
solution: Normalize feature statistics across channels per sample rather than across batch items.

pros: Independent of mini-batch size
Stabilizes deep Transformer training dynamics
cons: Requires elementwise gain (gamma) and bias (beta) parameters

name: Residual Skip Connection
summary: Identity mapping shortcut wrapping each attention and feed-forward sub-layer to enable gradient flow.
description: Residual skip connections add input x directly to sub-layer output SubLayer(x). This creates direct identity pathways for unimpeded backpropagation gradient propagation through deep Transformer stacks.
problem: Vanishing gradients and feature degradation across 12 to 96+ stacked attention sub-layers.
solution: Add identity shortcut connections around every sub-layer block.

pros: Eliminates vanishing gradient barrier in deep architectures
Preserves un-transformed feature identity across layers
cons: Requires matching feature dimensions d_model across all sub-layers

codeSnippet:
# Sub-layer residual wrapper pattern
x = x + self.sublayer(self.norm(x))

name: Masked Self-Attention
summary: Self-attention variant applying a causal mask to enforce autoregressive generation constraints.
description: Masked self-attention prevents position i from attending to positions > i by adding negative infinity (-inf) to attention logits before softmax evaluation.
math: MaskedAttention(Q, K, V) = Softmax( (Q*K^T)/sqrt(d_k) + M ) * V, M_{ij} = 0 if i>=j else -inf
problem: Information leakage from target tokens during causal sequence pre-training and decoding.
solution: Set upper-triangular logits of attention matrix to -infinity prior to softmax computation.

pros: Enforces strict causal order during parallel training
Enables autoregressive text generation
cons: Restricts attention receptive field to historical context only

papers: Attention Is All You Need (Vaswani et al., 2017)
codeSnippet:
mask = torch.triu(torch.full((seq_len, seq_len), float('-inf')), diagonal=1)
scores = scores + mask

name: Input & Token Embedding
summary: Lookup table mapping discrete token vocabulary indices to continuous d_model-dimensional vectors.
description: Token embedding layers convert categorical vocabulary tokens into dense vector space representations. Weights are scaled by sqrt(d_model) before adding positional encodings.
problem: Discrete token indices cannot undergo vector calculus or gradient optimization.
solution: Map indices to continuous trainable d_model dimensional vector lookup matrices.

pros: Dense continuous semantic representation space
Trainable end-to-end
cons: Memory footprint grows linearly with vocabulary size V * d_model

papers: Attention Is All You Need (Vaswani et al., 2017)

name: Linear Output Projection
summary: Linear layer projecting decoder hidden states to vocabulary probability distributions via softmax.
description: The Output Projection converts d_model dimensional final hidden representations into logit vectors over the full vocabulary size V, followed by softmax for next-token probability distribution generation.
problem: Converting continuous hidden states into categorical probability distributions over token vocabularies.
solution: Linear projection to size V with softmax normalization.

pros: Computes exact probability distribution over target vocabulary
cons: Computational bottleneck at large vocabulary sizes (e.g. 50k - 100k+ tokens)

papers: Attention Is All You Need (Vaswani et al., 2017)
